summary.one_liner: A satirical esoteric "perfect programming language" (renamed Gulf of Mexico) whose README jokingly describes its features, which are not real working functionality.
summary.what_it_does: The README presents a joke language called Gulf of Mexico (formerly DreamBerd) and describes its features in a satirical way: statements end with exclamation marks, the "not" operator is a semicolon, arrays start at -1, there are no loops, and parentheses are replaced by whitespace. It also covers mock features such as lifetimes for variables, file splitting with equals-sign lines, a single-instance class rule, and an AI feature that auto-emails incomplete code to the author. The README says the compiler stopped working in 2023 and that only a partial implementation existed as of 2024. Many sections are explicit jokes or political asides, so the text should not be read as a specification.
use_cases: reading a satirical programming language joke
finding an example of a deliberately absurd language spec
notable: Satirical language spec: exclamation marks end statements, semicolon as 'not' operator
Arrays start at -1, described as best of both 0- and 1-based indexing
Parentheses are ignored and replaced with whitespace
Explicitly says there are no loops and the compiler is no longer functional
Formerly named DreamBerd, now renamed Gulf of Mexico
caveats: Satirical: most features are jokes and do not work as described
README says the compiler is no longer functional (as of 2023); only a partial implementation existed as of 2024
No installation that works as documented; the install instructions are a joke
